correctness.rationale: For all n≥3, φ(n) is even, so each orbit enters odd states ≥5; initial n=1,2 pass through 4 to 5. For composite m, least prime q≤sqrt(m) gives φ(m)≤m−sqrt(m). Hence odd composite m≥27 decreases in one step. For odd prime p≥29, if p+2 composite, F²(p)≤p+5−sqrt(p+2)<p; otherwise p and p+2 are primes, so 3 divides p+4 and F³(p)≤2(p+4)/3+3<p. Therefore every odd state ≥27 strictly descends to a smaller odd state in ≤3 steps, forcing eventual entry into the positive finite invariant E={5,7,...,25}. All 11 exact transitions are supplied and have only cycles (9), (11,13,15), (23,25); none beyond the list is possible. Since the 23↔25 cycle persists, the universal eventual bound is optimally 25. Code checked initial values 1..200000, but the infinite proof does not depend on enumeration.

value.rationale: An explicit literature-motivated natural complete classification, not a single parameter-table entry: the earliest small odd shift already has three distinct periods, yet the published general theorem leaves their complete count and terminal bound unspecified. Proving from first principles that every positive orbit enters exactly eleven possible terminal states yields all cycles and the sharp global invariant 25. The prime-composite descent argument is useful for investigating other small shifts. No basin density, general k classification, or unproved consequence is asserted.
